verses.1:1: God, having spoken long ago in many portions and in many ways to the fathers by the prophets,
verses.1:2: has at the end of these days spoken to us by a Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom also He made the ages;
verses.1:3: who, being the radiance of His glory and the exact impress of His essence, and sustaining all things by the word of His power, having made purification for sins, sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
verses.1:4: having become by so much superior to the angels as He has inherited a name more excellent than theirs.
verses.1:5: For to which of the angels did He at any time say, "You are My Son; this day I have begotten You," and again, "I shall be a Father to Him, and He shall be a Son to Me"?
verses.1:6: And when He again brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, He says, "And let all the angels of God worship Him."
verses.1:7: And concerning the angels He says, "He who makes His angels spirits and His ministers a flame of fire."
verses.1:8: But to the Son He says, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of His kingdom.
verses.1:9: You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of exultation above Your companions."
verses.1:10: And, "You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the works of Your hands.
verses.1:11: They shall perish, yet You remain; and they all shall grow old like a garment,
verses.1:12: and like a mantle You shall roll them up, like a garment they shall also be changed; but You are the same, and Your years shall not fail."
verses.1:13: But to which of the angels has He ever said, "Sit at My right hand until I set Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet"?
verses.1:14: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth for service on behalf of those who are to inherit salvation?
verses.2:1: For this reason we must pay much more earnest attention to the things we have heard, lest at any time we drift away.
verses.2:2: For if the message spoken through angels stood firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,
verses.2:3: how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation, which, having at the first been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard,
verses.2:4: while God also bore witness with them both by signs and wonders, and by various mighty works, and by distributions of the Holy Spirit according to His own will?
verses.2:5: For it was not to angels that He subjected the inhabited world to come, of which we are speaking.
verses.2:6: But one has testified somewhere, saying, "What is man that You remember him, or a son of man that You care for him?
verses.2:7: You made him for a little while lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor;
verses.2:8: You subjected all things beneath his feet." For in subjecting all things to him, He left nothing that is not subjected to him. Yet at present we do not yet see all things subjected to him.
verses.2:9: But we behold Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.
verses.2:10: For it was fitting for Him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, in bringing many sons to glory, to perfect through sufferings the pioneer of their salvation.
verses.2:11: For both He who sanctifies and those who are being sanctified are all of one; for which reason He is not ashamed to call them brethren,
verses.2:12: saying, "I will proclaim Your name to My brethren; in the midst of the congregation I will praise You in song."
verses.2:13: And again, "I will place My trust in Him." And again, "Behold, I and the children whom God has given Me."
verses.2:14: Since therefore the children have shared in blood and flesh, He Himself likewise partook of the same, that through death He might render powerless him who holds the dominion of death, that is, the devil,
verses.2:15: and deliver all those who through fear of death were throughout their entire lifetime subject to bondage.
verses.2:16: For assuredly He does not come to the aid of angels, but He comes to the aid of the seed of Abraham.
verses.2:17: Therefore He was obligated in every respect to be made like His brethren, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
verses.2:18: For because He Himself has suffered in being tempted, He is able to come to the aid of those who are being tempted.
verses.3:1: Therefore, holy brethren, sharers in a heavenly calling, consider carefully the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Jesus,
verses.3:2: who was faithful to Him who appointed Him, just as Moses also was in His house.
verses.3:3: For this One has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, by as much as he who built the house has greater honor than the house.
verses.3:4: For every house is constructed by someone, yet He who constructed all things is God.
verses.3:5: And Moses indeed was faithful in all His house as a servant, for a testimony of the things that were to be spoken,
verses.3:6: but Christ as a Son over His house; whose house we are, if we hold fast the boldness and the boasting of our hope.
verses.3:7: Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear His voice,
verses.3:8: do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
verses.3:9: where your fathers tested Me by trial and saw My works
verses.3:10: for forty years. Therefore I was indignant with this generation, and I said, 'They always go astray in their heart, and they have not known My ways.'
verses.3:11: As I swore in My wrath, 'They shall never enter My rest.'"
verses.3:12: Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief in falling away from the living God;
verses.3:13: but exhort one another day by day, as long as it is called "Today," lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
verses.3:14: For we have become sharers in Christ, if indeed we hold fast our original assurance firm to the end,
verses.3:15: while it is said, "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion."
verses.3:16: For who, having heard, rebelled? Indeed, was it not all those who came out of Egypt through Moses?
verses.3:17: And with whom was He indignant for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
verses.3:18: And to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, except to those who disobeyed?
verses.3:19: And we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.
verses.4:1: Let us therefore fear, lest while a promise remains of entering into His rest, any among you should appear to have fallen short.
verses.4:2: For indeed we have had the good news proclaimed to us just as they also did; yet the word they heard did not profit them, since they were not united by faith with those who heard.
verses.4:3: For we who have believed enter into rest, just as He has said, "As I swore in My wrath, 'They shall not enter into My rest,'" although the works were accomplished from the foundation of the world.
verses.4:4: For He has spoken somewhere concerning the seventh day in this manner: "And God rested on the seventh day from all His works";
verses.4:5: and in this passage again: "They shall not enter into My rest."
verses.4:6: Since therefore it remains for some to enter into it, and those to whom the good news was formerly proclaimed did not enter because of disobedience,
verses.4:7: He again appoints a certain day, "Today," speaking through David after so long a time, just as it has been spoken beforehand: "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts."
verses.4:8: For if Joshua had given them rest, He would not have spoken afterward concerning another day.
verses.4:9: So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God.
verses.4:10: For the one who has entered into His rest has himself also rested from his works, just as God did from His own.
verses.4:11: Let us therefore strive earnestly to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall in the same pattern of disobedience.
verses.4:12: For the word of God is living and effective, and keener than every two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is a judge of the thoughts and purposes of the heart.
verses.4:13: And no creature is unseen before Him, but all things are naked and laid bare to the eyes of Him to whom we must render an account.
verses.4:14: Having therefore a great High Priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to our confession.
verses.4:15: For we do not have a High Priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but One who has been tempted in all things in like manner, yet without sin.
verses.4:16: Let us therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for timely help.
verses.5:1: For every high priest taken from among men is appointed on behalf of men in matters pertaining to God, so that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,
verses.5:2: being able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and wandering astray, since he himself is also beset with weakness.
verses.5:3: And because of it he is obligated, just as for the people, so also for himself, to make offering for sins.
verses.5:4: And no one takes this honor for himself, but only when called by God, just as Aaron also was.
verses.5:5: So also Christ did not glorify Himself to become a High Priest, but it was He who spoke to Him: "You are My Son; today I have begotten You";
verses.5:6: just as He also says in another passage: "You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek."
verses.5:7: In the days of His flesh, He offered up both petitions and supplications, with loud crying and tears, to Him who was able to save Him from death, and He was heard because of His godly reverence;
verses.5:8: although He was a Son, He learned obedience from the things which He suffered.
verses.5:9: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him,
verses.5:10: designated by God as a High Priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.5:11: Concerning this we have much to speak, and it is difficult to explain, since you have become sluggish in hearing.
verses.5:12: For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you again have need for someone to teach you the elementary principles of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have come to need milk, and not solid food.
verses.5:13: For everyone who partakes of milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is an infant.
verses.5:14: But solid food belongs to the mature, to those who through practice have their faculties trained for the discernment of both good and evil.
verses.6:1: Therefore, leaving behind the elementary word concerning Christ, let us press on toward maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,
verses.6:2: instruction concerning washings, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
verses.6:3: And this we will do, if indeed God permits.
verses.6:4: For it is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and have become sharers of the Holy Spirit,
verses.6:5: and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the coming age,
verses.6:6: and then have fallen away, to be renewed again to repentance, crucifying afresh for themselves the Son of God and holding Him up to public disgrace.
verses.6:7: For land that drinks in the rain which often falls upon it, and brings forth vegetation useful to those for whose sake it is tilled, partakes of blessing from God;
verses.6:8: but if it yields thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near to a curse, whose end is to be burned.
verses.6:9: Yet, beloved, concerning you we are convinced of better things—things that accompany salvation—even though we speak in this manner.
verses.6:10: For God is not unjust so as to forget your work and the love which you have shown toward His name, in having ministered to the saints and in continuing to minister.
verses.6:11: And we earnestly desire that each one of you show the same diligence for the full assurance of hope until the end,
verses.6:12: so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
verses.6:13: For when God gave a promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater by whom He could swear, He swore by Himself,
verses.6:14: saying, "Assuredly, blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you."
verses.6:15: And thus, having waited patiently, he obtained the promise.
verses.6:16: For men swear by one who is greater, and among them an oath for confirmation puts an end to all dispute.
verses.6:17: In the same way, God, desiring all the more to show to the heirs of the promise the immutability of His counsel, interposed with an oath,
verses.6:18: so that through two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge may have strong encouragement to lay hold of the hope set before us.
verses.6:19: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both secure and steadfast, entering into the inner place behind the veil,
verses.6:20: where as a forerunner on our behalf Jesus has entered, having become a High Priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.7:1: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham as he returned from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
verses.7:2: to whom Abraham also apportioned a tenth of all, being by interpretation first king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace,
verses.7:3: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, yet made to resemble the Son of God, abides a priest for all time.
verses.7:4: Now observe how great this man was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth from the choicest spoils.
verses.7:5: And indeed those among the sons of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment to collect tithes from the people according to the law, that is, from their brethren, though they have come forth from the loins of Abraham;
verses.7:6: yet he whose genealogy is not traced from them received a tithe from Abraham and blessed the one who held the promises.
verses.7:7: And beyond all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
verses.7:8: And here men who die receive tithes, but there one of whom it is witnessed that he lives.
verses.7:9: And, so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, paid tithes,
verses.7:10: for he was still in his father's loins when Melchizedek met him.
verses.7:11: Now if perfection had come through the Levitical priesthood—for on the basis of it the people received the law—what further need would there have been for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be designated according to the order of Aaron?
verses.7:12: For when the priesthood is changed, of necessity there takes place a change of the law as well.
verses.7:13: For the One of whom these things are spoken belonged to another tribe, from which no one has attended at the altar;
verses.7:14: for it is clearly evident that our Lord has sprung from Judah, concerning which tribe Moses spoke nothing of priests.
verses.7:15: And it is even more abundantly clear if another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
verses.7:16: who has become such not according to a law of fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life,
verses.7:17: for it is testified, "You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek."
verses.7:18: For on the one hand, there is a setting aside of the former commandment because of its weakness and unprofitableness—
verses.7:19: for the law perfected nothing—and on the other hand, the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
verses.7:20: And by as much as this was not without an oath—for those others indeed became priests without an oath,
verses.7:21: but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, "The Lord has sworn and will not relent, 'You are a priest forever'"—
verses.7:22: by so much Jesus has also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
verses.7:23: Moreover, those priests have been many in number, because death prevented them from remaining in office;
verses.7:24: but He, because He abides forever, holds an unchangeable priesthood;
verses.7:25: Therefore He is also able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He ever lives to intercede on their behalf.
verses.7:26: For such a High Priest was indeed fitting for us—holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted higher than the heavens;
verses.7:27: who has no need day by day, like the high priests, to offer up sacrifices first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people—for this He did once for all when He offered up Himself.
verses.7:28: For the law appoints as high priests men who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son who has been perfected forever.
verses.8:1: Now the chief point of the things we are saying is this: we have such a High Priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
verses.8:2: a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man.
verses.8:3: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore it is necessary for this One also to have something to offer.
verses.8:4: Now if He were on earth, He would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to the law;
verses.8:5: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to construct the tabernacle; for He says, "See that you make all things according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain."
verses.8:6: But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as He is also the Mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted upon better promises.
verses.8:7: For if that first covenant had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second;
verses.8:8: for finding fault with them, He says, "Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah—
verses.8:9: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they did not abide in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
verses.8:10: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will place My laws into their mind, and upon their hearts I will inscribe them; and I shall be their God, and they shall be My people.
verses.8:11: And they shall by no means teach each one his fellow citizen, and each one his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' for all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
verses.8:12: For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and their sins I will never remember again."
verses.8:13: In speaking of a "new" covenant, He has made the first obsolete; and what is becoming obsolete and growing old is near to vanishing away.
verses.9:1: Now indeed the first covenant had ordinances of worship and an earthly sanctuary.
verses.9:2: For a tabernacle was prepared: the first section, in which were the lampstand, the table, and the bread of the Presence, which is called the Holy Place;
verses.9:3: and behind the second veil, the tabernacle called the Holy of Holies,
verses.9:4: having a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant overlaid on every side with gold, in which were a golden jar containing the manna, Aaron's rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;
verses.9:5: and above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. Concerning these things we cannot now speak in detail.
verses.9:6: Now with these things thus prepared, the priests continually enter the first tabernacle, performing their sacred services;
verses.9:7: but into the second the high priest alone enters once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people's sins of ignorance,
verses.9:8: by this the Holy Spirit signifies that the way into the sanctuary has not yet been made manifest while the first tabernacle still has its standing,
verses.9:9: which is a symbol for the present time; according to it both gifts and sacrifices are offered that are unable to make the worshiper perfect in conscience,
verses.9:10: dealing only with foods and drinks and various washings, ordinances of the flesh imposed until a time of reformation.
verses.9:11: But when Christ appeared as High Priest of the good things that have come, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands—that is, not of this creation—
verses.9:12: and not by means of the blood of goats and calves, but by means of His own blood, He entered once for all into the sanctuary, having secured eternal redemption.
verses.9:13: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the purification of the flesh,
verses.9:14: how much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without blemish to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
verses.9:15: And for this reason He is the Mediator of a new covenant, so that, since a death has taken place for the redemption of the transgressions under the first covenant, those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
verses.9:16: For where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must of necessity be established;
verses.9:17: for a will is confirmed only upon death, since it is never in force while the one who made it lives.
verses.9:18: Therefore not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.
verses.9:19: For when every commandment according to the law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
verses.9:20: saying, "This is the blood of the covenant which God has enjoined upon you."
verses.9:21: And in the same manner he sprinkled with the blood both the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry.
verses.9:22: And almost all things are cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
verses.9:23: Therefore it was necessary for the copies of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
verses.9:24: For Christ did not enter a sanctuary made with hands, a counterpart of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf;
verses.9:25: nor was it that He should offer Himself repeatedly, as the high priest enters the sanctuary year by year with blood that is not his own,
verses.9:26: for then He would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world; but now, once at the consummation of the ages, He has been manifested to put away sin through the sacrifice of Himself.
verses.9:27: And just as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this comes judgment,
verses.9:28: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, shall appear a second time, apart from sin, to those who eagerly await Him, for salvation.
verses.10:1: For the law, having a shadow of the coming good things and not the very image of those realities, is never able, with the same sacrifices which they offer continually year after year, to make perfect those who draw near.
verses.10:2: For otherwise, would they not have ceased being offered, because the worshipers, having been purified once, would have no further consciousness of sins?
verses.10:3: Yet in them there is a remembrance of sins year by year.
verses.10:4: For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and of goats should remove sins.
verses.10:5: Therefore, as He enters into the world, He says, "Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, yet a body You prepared for Me.
verses.10:6: In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You took no delight.
verses.10:7: Then I said, 'Behold, I have come—in the scroll of the book it stands written concerning Me—to do Your will, O God.'"
verses.10:8: When He says above, "Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin You did not desire, nor did You delight in them"—which are offered according to the law—
verses.10:9: then He has said, "Behold, I have come to do Your will." He does away with the first in order that He may establish the second.
verses.10:10: By that will we stand sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
verses.10:11: And indeed every priest stands day after day ministering and offering time and again the same sacrifices, which are never able to take away sins.
verses.10:12: But this One, having offered a single sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
verses.10:13: waiting from that time onward until His enemies are set as a footstool for His feet.
verses.10:14: For by a single offering He has brought to perfection for all time those who are being sanctified.
verses.10:15: And the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us; for after having said,
verses.10:16: "This is the covenant that I will establish with them after those days," the Lord says, "I will put My laws upon their hearts, and upon their mind I will inscribe them,
verses.10:17: and their sins and their iniquities I will never again remember."
verses.10:18: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin.
verses.10:19: Therefore, brethren, since we have boldness to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,
verses.10:20: by that new and living way which He dedicated for us through the veil, that is to say, His flesh,
verses.10:21: and since we have a great Priest over the house of God,
verses.10:22: let us draw near with a genuine heart in complete assurance of faith, our hearts having been sprinkled from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
verses.10:23: Let us hold firm the confession of our hope unwaveringly, for faithful is He who promised.
verses.10:24: And let us take careful thought for one another, to spur on love and good works,
verses.10:25: not abandoning our own assembling together, as is the custom of some, but exhorting one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.
verses.10:26: For if we willfully keep on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains any longer,
verses.10:27: but rather a certain dreadful expectation of judgment and a fury of fire that is about to devour the adversaries.
verses.10:28: Whoever sets aside the law of Moses dies without mercy upon the testimony of two or three witnesses.
verses.10:29: Of how much severer punishment, do you suppose, will he be judged worthy who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and has regarded as profane the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and has outraged the Spirit of grace?
verses.10:30: For we know Him who has said, "Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay," and again, "The Lord shall judge His people."
verses.10:31: It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
verses.10:32: Yet call to remembrance the earlier days, in which, after you had been enlightened, you endured a great conflict of sufferings:
verses.10:33: on the one hand being made a public spectacle through both reproaches and afflictions, and on the other hand becoming partners with those who were dealt with in this manner.
verses.10:34: For you showed sympathy to those in bonds, and with joy you accepted the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you yourselves have a better and abiding possession.
verses.10:35: Therefore do not cast aside your boldness, which carries a great reward.
verses.10:36: For you stand in need of endurance, so that, after doing the will of God, you may obtain the promise.
verses.10:37: For "yet a very little while, He who is coming shall come and will not tarry;
verses.10:38: but My righteous one shall live by faith; and if he shrinks back, My soul takes no delight in him."
verses.10:39: Yet we do not belong to those who shrink back to destruction, but to those who have faith for the preserving of the soul.
verses.11:1: Now faith is the firm assurance of things hoped for, the certain proof of things unseen.
verses.11:2: For by this the elders received a good testimony.
verses.11:3: By faith we understand that the ages were fashioned by the word of God, so that what is seen did not come into being out of things that are visible.
verses.11:4: By faith Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain, through which he received testimony that he was righteous, as God bore witness concerning his gifts; and through it, though he has died, he still speaks.
verses.11:5: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him up; for before he was taken up, he had received testimony that he had pleased God.
verses.11:6: And without faith it is impossible to please Him; for the one who draws near to God must believe that He exists and that He becomes a rewarder of those who earnestly seek Him.
verses.11:7: By faith Noah, having been divinely warned concerning things not yet seen, moved with reverent fear, constructed an ark for the salvation of his household, by which he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that is according to faith.
verses.11:8: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to a place that he was about to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.
verses.11:9: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign land, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the fellow heirs of the same promise;
verses.11:10: for he was waiting for the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God.
verses.11:11: By faith, even with Sarah herself, he received strength to beget offspring, even beyond the proper time of age, because he considered Him faithful who had promised.
verses.11:12: Therefore from one man, and him as good as dead, there sprang offspring as many as the stars of heaven in multitude, and like the innumerable sand by the shore of the sea.
verses.11:13: All these died in faith, not having received the promises, yet having seen them from afar and welcomed them, and having confessed that they were strangers and sojourners upon the earth.
verses.11:14: For those who say such things make clear that they are seeking a homeland.
verses.11:15: And indeed, if they had been thinking of that land from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.
verses.11:16: But as it is, they long for a better one, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God; for He has prepared a city for them.
verses.11:17: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac; and he who had welcomed the promises was offering up his only begotten son,
verses.11:18: to whom it was spoken, "In Isaac your offspring shall be called,"
verses.11:19: reckoning that God is able to raise him even from the dead, from which, in a figure, he also received him back.
verses.11:20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.
verses.11:21: By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshiped leaning upon the top of his staff.
verses.11:22: By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave charge concerning his bones.
verses.11:23: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was fair, and they did not fear the edict of the king.
verses.11:24: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
verses.11:25: choosing rather to endure mistreatment together with the people of God than to have the fleeting enjoyment of sin,
verses.11:26: considering the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.
verses.11:27: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king; for he stood steadfast as seeing Him who is invisible.
verses.11:28: By faith he observed the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, lest the destroyer of the firstborn should touch them.
verses.11:29: By faith they crossed the Red Sea as through dry land; and when the Egyptians attempted the same, they were swallowed up.
verses.11:30: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, having been encircled for seven days.
verses.11:31: By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who were disobedient, having welcomed the spies in peace.
verses.11:32: And what more shall I say? For time will fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, and of David and Samuel and the prophets,
verses.11:33: who through faith conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
verses.11:34: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight.
verses.11:35: Women received back their dead by resurrection; and others were tortured, refusing to accept release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
verses.11:36: Still others experienced mockings and scourgings, and moreover chains and imprisonment.
verses.11:37: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were tested, they died by the slaughter of the sword; they went about in sheepskins and in goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, mistreated—
verses.11:38: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts and mountains, and in caves and dens of the earth.
verses.11:39: And all these, though they received a good testimony through faith, did not receive the promise,
verses.11:40: since God had provided beforehand something better for us, so that apart from us they should not be made perfect.
verses.12:1: Therefore we also, having so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, laying aside every burden and the sin that so easily entangles us, let us run with perseverance the race that lies before us,
verses.12:2: fixing our eyes upon Jesus, the founder and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning the shame, and has taken His seat at the right hand of the throne of God.
verses.12:3: For consider Him who has endured such hostility from sinners against themselves, lest you grow weary and faint in your souls.
verses.12:4: You have not yet resisted to the point of blood, contending against sin,
verses.12:5: and you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: "My son, do not make light of the discipline of the Lord, nor lose heart when you are reproved by Him;
verses.12:6: for the Lord disciplines the one whom He loves, and He scourges every son whom He receives."
verses.12:7: Endure for the sake of discipline; God deals with you as with sons. For what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
verses.12:8: But if you are without discipline, in which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
verses.12:9: Furthermore, we had fathers of our flesh who disciplined us, and we respected them; shall we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits and live?
verses.12:10: For they disciplined us for a few days as seemed good to them, but He does so for our benefit, that we may share in His holiness.
verses.12:11: Now all discipline seems for the present not to be a matter of joy, but of sorrow; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
verses.12:12: Therefore lift up the drooping hands and the weakened knees,
verses.12:13: and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be put out of joint, but rather may be healed.
verses.12:14: Pursue peace with all, and the sanctification without which no one will see the Lord,
verses.12:15: watching carefully lest anyone fall short of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up cause trouble, and by it many be defiled;
verses.12:16: lest there be any immoral or profane person like Esau, who for a single meal sold his own birthright.
verses.12:17: For you know that afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place for repentance, though he earnestly sought it with tears.
verses.12:18: For you have not drawn near to what may be touched, and to blazing fire, and to darkness, and gloom, and tempest,
verses.12:19: and to the blast of a trumpet and a voice of words, whose hearers pleaded that no further message be spoken to them;
verses.12:20: for they could not bear the command that was given: "Even if a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned."
verses.12:21: And so fearful was the sight that Moses said, "I am terrified and trembling."
verses.12:22: Rather, you have drawn near to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels in festive gathering,
verses.12:23: and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, the Judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
verses.12:24: and to Jesus, the Mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better than Abel.
verses.12:25: See that you do not refuse Him who is speaking. For if those did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, much less shall we escape if we turn away from Him who warns from heaven,
verses.12:26: whose voice shook the earth at that time; but now He has promised, saying, "Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also heaven."
verses.12:27: Now this phrase, "Yet once more," signifies the removal of the things that are shaken, as of things that have been made, so that the things which cannot be shaken may remain.
verses.12:28: Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us have gratitude, through which we may offer acceptable worship to God with reverence and awe,
verses.12:29: for indeed our God is a consuming fire.
verses.13:2: Do not forget hospitality to strangers, for through it some have entertained angels without knowing it.
verses.13:3: Remember those who are in bonds as though bound with them, and those who are mistreated, since you yourselves are also in the body.
verses.13:4: Let marriage be honored among all, and let the marriage bed remain undefiled; for God will judge fornicators and adulterers.
verses.13:5: Let your conduct be free from the love of money, being content with what you have; for He Himself has said, "I will by no means leave you, nor will I ever forsake you."
verses.13:6: So we may say with confidence, "The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear; what shall man do to me?"
verses.13:7: Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you; considering closely the outcome of their manner of life, imitate their faith.
verses.13:8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today, and forevermore.
verses.13:9: Do not be carried away by diverse and strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be established by grace, not by foods, by which those who walk in them have not profited.
verses.13:10: We have an altar from which those who minister at the tabernacle have no authority to eat.
verses.13:11: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is carried into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin are burned up outside the camp.
verses.13:12: Therefore Jesus also, in order that He might sanctify the people through His own blood, suffered outside the gate.
verses.13:13: Let us then go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach.
verses.13:14: For here we do not have an abiding city, but we earnestly seek the one that is to come.
verses.13:15: Through Him, therefore, let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess His name.
verses.13:16: And do not forget to do good and to share with others, for God is well pleased with such sacrifices.
verses.13:17: Obey your leaders and yield to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who shall render an account, so that they may do this with joy and not with groaning; for that would be unprofitable to you.
verses.13:18: Pray for us, for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, desiring to conduct ourselves honorably in all things.
verses.13:19: And I exhort you all the more earnestly to do this, so that I may be restored to you the more quickly.
verses.13:20: Now may the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep through the blood of the eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,
verses.13:21: equip you in every good thing to do His will, working in us what is well-pleasing before Him through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.13:22: Now I urge you, brethren, bear patiently with the word of exhortation, for indeed I have written to you briefly.
verses.13:23: Know that our brother Timothy has been released, with whom, if he comes soon, I shall see you.
verses.13:24: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those who are from Italy greet you.
verses.13:25: May grace be with you all.

notes.1:6: The adverb "again" (palin) may modify "brings" (pointing to a second entry or return into the inhabited world) or "says" (introducing another Scripture quotation, as in 1:5).
notes.1:8: The Greek text reads "of His kingdom" (tes basileias autou) rather than "of Your kingdom" (as in Psalm 45:6 / 44:7 LXX and some manuscripts).
notes.1:12: The Greek text includes "like a garment" (hos himation) before "they shall also be changed," echoing 1:11.
notes.2:7: The phrase brachy ti may mean "for a little while" (temporal, fitting 2:9) or "a little" (in degree); the Greek text here also follows the shorter reading without "and set him over the works of Your hands."
notes.2:9: The Greek text reads chariti theou ("by the grace of God"); a small number of witnesses read choris theou ("apart from God").
notes.2:16: The verb epilambanetai literally means "takes hold of," used here in the sense of laying hold of someone in order to rescue or aid.
notes.3:6: The Greek text omits "firm to the end" here (words that appear in 3:14).
notes.3:9: The Greek text reads "tested ... by trial" (without an explicit object pronoun "Me") and connects "for forty years" (3:10) with "saw My works" rather than with God's indignation.
notes.3:11: The Greek particle ei ("if") reflects the Hebrew oath idiom of Psalm 95:11, functioning as an emphatic negative ("They shall never enter").
notes.3:14: The noun hypostasis (rendered "essence" in 1:3) is used here in the sense of firm assurance or confidence.
notes.4:2: The critical Greek text reads the accusative plural participle synkekerasmenous ("since they were not united by faith with those who heard"), whereas some later manuscripts read the nominative singular referring to the message ("not being mixed with faith in those who heard").
notes.4:3: The Greek quotation follows the Septuagint's Hebraic oath formula (literally "If they shall enter"), which carries the force of an emphatic negative: "They shall not enter."
notes.4:8: The Greek text reads Iesous, the Septuagint equivalent of the Hebrew name Joshua, referring here to Joshua son of Nun who led Israel into Canaan.
notes.4:13: "Laid bare" translates tetrachelismena, literally "bent back by the neck" so as to be fully exposed; the verse also concludes with a play on logos ("word" in v. 12, "account" here).
notes.5:7: The phrase apo tes eulabeias is best understood as "because of His godly reverence" (referring to His pious submission to the Father), though some interpret it as deliverance "from His fear."
notes.5:8: The Greek preserves a striking paronomasia between emathen ("learned") and epathen ("suffered").
notes.5:12: The Greek text accents tina as the indefinite pronoun ("that someone teach you"); an alternative interrogative accentuation yields "what are the elementary principles."
notes.6:2: The critical Greek text has accusative didachen ("instruction") in apposition to "foundation" (v. 1), and plural baptismon ("washings"), which elsewhere in Hebrews (9:10) denotes ceremonial washings and here may encompass ritual washings and baptisms.
notes.6:6: The present participles ("crucifying ... and holding Him up") leave open whether the clause states the reason renewal is impossible ("since") or its duration ("while"); anastaurountas can denote either "crucifying afresh" or simply "crucifying."
notes.6:10: The critical Greek text reads "your work and the love," without the later textual addition "labor of" before "love."
notes.7:17: The critical text reads passive martyreitai ("it is testified"), whereas some later manuscripts read active martyrei ("He testifies").
notes.7:21: The critical text ends the quotation from Psalm 110:4 at "forever"; later manuscripts add "according to the order of Melchizedek."
notes.7:25: Greek eis to panteles carries both a qualitative sense ("completely" or "to the uttermost") and a temporal sense ("for all time").
notes.8:8: The dative autois ("them") may modify either "finding fault" ("finding fault with them, He says") or "says" ("finding fault, He says to them").
notes.8:9: Following the Septuagint of Jeremiah 38:32 (MT 31:32), Greek emelesa auton reads "I disregarded them" rather than the Masoretic Hebrew "though I was a husband to them."
notes.8:11: The critical text reads politen ("fellow citizen") rather than the later manuscript variant plesion ("neighbor").
notes.8:12: The critical text reads only "their sins" and omits the later manuscript expansion "and their lawless deeds."
notes.9:4: Greek thymiaterion can denote either the "altar of incense" (associated with the inner sanctuary on the Day of Atonement) or a "censer."
notes.9:11: The critical text reads ton genomenon agathon ("the good things that have come"), whereas other manuscripts read mellonton ("the good things to come").
notes.9:14: The critical text reads hymon ("your conscience"), whereas other manuscripts read hemon ("our conscience").
notes.9:16: Greek diatheke means both "covenant" (9:15, 20) and "will" or "testament" (9:16–17), a dual meaning the author uses to link Christ's death with the inauguration of the new covenant.
notes.10:5: Quoting Psalm 39:7 LXX (40:6 MT), the Greek text reads "a body You prepared for Me," reflecting the Septuagint rendering rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "ears You have opened for me."
notes.10:12: The Greek phrase for "for all time" (eis to dienekes) stands between the two clauses and can modify either "having offered a single sacrifice for sins" (as translated here) or "sat down at the right hand of God."
notes.10:34: The critical Greek text reads "those in bonds" (the prisoners) rather than the later variant "my chains," and does not include "in heaven" after "a better and abiding possession."
notes.10:38: Following the Septuagint of Habakkuk 2:4, the critical text includes the pronoun "My" ("My righteous one," omitted in some later manuscripts) and links "if he shrinks back" directly to "shrink back" in verse 39.
notes.11:11: The Greek text reads the dative 'αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ' ("with Sarah herself"), keeping Abraham as the subject who received strength to beget offspring ('καταβολὴν σπέρματος'); other manuscripts read the nominative, making Sarah the subject who received strength to conceive.
notes.11:21: Follows the Septuagint of Genesis 47:31 ("the top of his staff"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic vocalization reads "the head of his bed."
notes.11:37: The Greek text retains 'ἐπειράσθησαν' ("they were tested"), a word omitted in some early manuscripts.
notes.12:3: The Greek text reads the plural reflexive 'εἰς ἑαυτούς' ("against themselves"), highlighting that sinners' hostility toward Christ turns against themselves; other manuscripts read the singular, "against Himself."
notes.12:7: The Greek text reads 'εἰς παιδείαν' ("for the sake of discipline" or "it is for discipline that you endure"), whereas later manuscripts read the conditional 'εἰ' ("if").
notes.12:18: The Greek text omits the word "mountain" after "what may be touched," contrasting the tangible terrors of Sinai with Mount Zion in verse 22.
notes.12:28: The Greek idiom 'ἔχωμεν χάριν' means "let us have gratitude" (be thankful), though some understand it as "let us hold fast to grace."
notes.13:4: The opening Greek clauses contain no explicit verb and may be taken either imperatively ("Let marriage be honored") in keeping with the surrounding exhortations or declaratively ("Marriage is honored"); the text also reads "for" (gar) rather than "but" (de).
notes.13:10: Interpreters debate whether "altar" (thysiasterion) refers primarily to the cross, Christ's self-offering, or the heavenly sanctuary, contrasting the new-covenant sacrifice with the Levitical tabernacle service.
notes.13:21: The Greek text reads "in every good thing" (without "work") and "working in us" (hemin rather than "in you"); the closing doxology renders "to the ages of the ages" as "forever and ever."
notes.13:24: The phrase "Those who are from Italy" (hoi apo tes Italias) can mean either Italian believers currently abroad with the author or believers writing from within Italy.
